attempts.summary: Configured traffic mirroring so node3 receives a copy of all traffic node1 exchanges with node2 on their shared L2 segment, while that traffic itself keeps flowing unaffected. Implementation: node1's eth1, node2's ens7, and node3's ens7 form one shared broadcast segment (confirmed empirically - it behaves as a switch, not a hub: unicast node1<->node2 traffic was invisible to node3 before mirroring). Assigned static IPs on the segment (node1 192.168.50.1, node2 192.168.50.2, node3 192.168.50.3), built a GRETAP tunnel from node1 to node3, and installed Linux tc (clsact/flower/mirred) rules on node1's eth1 that mirror (not redirect) packets to/from node2's IP into the tunnel. Node3 decapsulates the tunnel on its local gretap1 interface, where a capture sees the original node1<->node2 packets (still addressed to each other) even though addressed elsewhere. Verified with tcpdump: 10/10 ICMP packets from a 5-ping exchange were mirrored to node3, while the original ping itself showed 0% loss throughout. Made the configuration persistent (systemd oneshot units on node1 and node3, ifupdown drop-in configs for the static IPs on node2/node3) since none of this state survives a reboot by default. Completed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol: captured a healthy baseline (boot IDs + working mirror) on all three nodes, then restarted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time (preserving the segment - no concurrent restarts), confirmed each node's boot ID changed post-restart, and re-verified after each restart that the mirroring service/config auto-recovered and the ping+tcpdump mirror test still passed end-to-end. All three nodes are now healthy with mirroring active and persistent.
